resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lighthouse Friends' visitor line says the Coast Guard owns the lighthouse, but its own history says the Historical Association has owned it since 2004. The Lighthouse Directory, the Preservation Society and the Coast Guard list ('Private aid') all describe a private owner, so the Historical Association is taken as the owner.

notes_for_editor: Keepers are Lighthouse Friends' roster (facts only), with one Department entry for Riley in 1906. The Department reports in the local corpus begin with fiscal 1900, so the 1889 construction and first lighting rest on three secondary sources that agree (Lighthouse Friends, Lighthouse Directory, Preservation Society). Lighthouse Friends says the Coast Guard owns the light; its own history and the other sources say the Historical Association does, and the Coast Guard list calls it a private aid. Milledge (1912) overlaps McMillan (1908-1913), unresolved. Gavaza appears in Department name lists for 1914-15 with no station on the same line, so he is not linked to Annapolis beyond Lighthouse Friends. No storm, wreck or rescue at this station was found in the sources read, so that chapter is omitted. Record ownership 'unknown' could read 'private' (Coast Guard list) or 'nonprofit'; this file does not change the record. The 1906 row for Riley ('Riley, Simon W Annapolis Mar.') is read from a single OCR line on scan 183 (printed 174); the page image was not viewed because the built-in browser refused archive.org, so the checker should confirm it before publication.
